TABLE.NAME: bento
TABLE.COMMENT: Each row is one Bento presentation activity instance

FIELD.NAME: course
FIELD.COMMENT: Course this activity belongs to

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Activity name shown on the course page

FIELD.NAME: intro
FIELD.COMMENT: Standard mod_intro description

FIELD.NAME: document
FIELD.COMMENT: The teacher's own bento/slides JSON document — LONGTEXT-equivalent, can hold embedded images. Still the ONLY document when allowstudentsubmissions is off; otherwise it's the teacher's own copy (e.g. an example/instructions deck) while students each get their own row in bento_submissions instead. LEGACY as of documentinfilestore's own introduction — see that field's comment for the current read/write path. Kept (not backfilled to empty) so a row already migrated still has its pre-migration text as a fallback if its file ever goes missing.

FIELD.NAME: documentinfilestore
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether this row's actual document content now lives in Moodle's own File API (component mod_bento, filearea document, itemid = this row's own id) instead of the `document` text column above. 0 (the default) means this row still only has the text-column copy — never yet saved through the file-storage path, or not yet migrated by db/upgrade.php. 1 means the file IS the current source of truth. bento_get_document() in lib.php is the one place that decides which of the two a given row is actually read from, so nothing else should read/write `document` or this column directly.

FIELD.NAME: documentvisible
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether the published document (this row's own document/file-storage content — NOT the activity itself) is currently shown to whoever views it. 1 (the default, so every existing activity keeps showing its document unchanged right after upgrade) means view.php's own classic/master-document display shows it normally. 0 means view.php shows a plain "no presentation currently available" message instead — the ACTIVITY itself stays exactly as visible/hidden as Moodle's own course_modules.visible setting already has it (this never touches that), which matters specifically for allowstudentsubmissions=1 activities: the submission gallery and every student's own submission stay fully reachable regardless of this flag, only the shared master document's own display is affected. Toggled via mod_bento_set_document_visible; a card in manage.php's own tile-import view surfaces this as an open/closed eye icon next to its title.

FIELD.NAME: grade
FIELD.COMMENT: Max points for the gradebook item; 0 = ungraded; negative = a scale id (standard Moodle convention)

FIELD.NAME: allowstudentsubmissions
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = classic single teacher-authored deck (v1 behaviour). 1 = each enrolled student creates/imports and edits their OWN presentation instead (bento_submissions).

FIELD.NAME: submissionvisibility
FIELD.COMMENT: Only meaningful when allowstudentsubmissions=1. 'auto' = every student can see every other student's submission immediately. 'moderated' = a submission is only visible to OTHER students once a teacher approves it (see bento_submissions.status); the owner can always see/edit their own regardless.

FIELD.NAME: duedate
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = no deadline. Once passed, a student (mod/bento:submit, no mod/bento:edit) can no longer save changes to their own submission — enforced in edit.php and the mod_bento_save_document web service, both server-side. Never restricts mod/bento:edit.

FIELD.NAME: duedatevisible
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether the deadline itself (not just its enforcement) is shown to students on the gallery page.

FIELD.NAME: loginonly
FIELD.COMMENT: Restricts the TEACHER's own master presentation to logged-in users even in a course that otherwise allows guest access. Student submissions (bento_submissions) are always login-only regardless of this flag — that restriction is unconditional, enforced directly in the pages that serve them, not tied to a per-instance setting at all.

FIELD.NAME: allowstudentpaste
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether STUDENTS get the 'Inhalte auf Folien verteilen' (paste-and-split) tile on submission_new.php — off by default even when allowstudentsubmissions is on. Copy-paste is tempting enough as a shortcut that a teacher should opt into offering it explicitly, rather than it being on by default alongside student submissions generally. Teachers themselves (mod_form.php) always get the tile regardless of this setting — it only ever gates the STUDENT-facing copy.

FIELD.NAME: maxdocumentsize
FIELD.COMMENT: Per-activity presentation size ceiling in megabytes for the teacher's own presentation (and draft decks) — also the fallback for student submissions when maxstudentdocumentsize is 0 (unset). Set from settings.php's own absolutemaxdocumentsize (a site-wide hard ceiling this can only ever be set BELOW, never above) at activity-creation time — see mod_form.php's own default and bento_effective_max_document_bytes() in lib.php, which enforces the smaller of the two on every save.

FIELD.NAME: maxstudentdocumentsize
FIELD.COMMENT: A SEPARATE size ceiling in megabytes for student submissions specifically — 0 (the default) means no separate limit, falling back to maxdocumentsize (the same limit the teacher's own document uses), matching every existing activity's own behaviour unchanged. When >0, bento_effective_max_document_bytes() uses this instead for a submission, still never exceeding the site-wide absolutemaxdocumentsize ceiling either way.

TABLE.NAME: bento_grades
TABLE.COMMENT: One manually-entered grade per student per bento instance

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student this grade is for

FIELD.NAME: grader
FIELD.COMMENT: The teacher who entered it

FIELD.NAME: published
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = draft, entered but hidden from the student (grade_grade.hidden=1 in the real gradebook too). 1 = published — visible to the student, same as classic mod_bento grading. Entering/changing a grade never publishes it by itself; only the explicit publish action does.

INDEX.NAME: bentoid-userid
INDEX.COMMENT: One grade row per student per instance

TABLE.NAME: bento_submissions
TABLE.COMMENT: One student-authored bento/slides document per student per instance — only used when bento.allowstudentsubmissions=1

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student who owns this submission — the only user allowed to edit it

FIELD.NAME: document
FIELD.COMMENT: The student's own bento/slides JSON document. LEGACY as of documentinfilestore's own introduction — see that field's comment for the current read/write path.

FIELD.NAME: documentinfilestore
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether this submission's actual content now lives in Moodle's own File API (component mod_bento, filearea BENTO_SUBMISSION_FILEAREA, itemid = this row's own id) instead of the `document` text column above — the same scheme bento.documentinfilestore already uses for the master document, applied here so a large submission (embedded images etc.) doesn't hit the same MySQL text-column-size ceiling the master document already moved off of. 0 (the default) means this row still only has the text-column copy. bento_get_document()/bento_put_document() in lib.php (with their own $filearea parameter) are the one place that decides which of the two a given row is actually read from.

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: 'pending' (awaiting teacher approval — only relevant in 'moderated' visibility mode) or 'approved'. Ignored entirely in 'auto' visibility mode, where every submission is visible regardless of this value.

INDEX.NAME: bentoid-userid
INDEX.COMMENT: Exactly one submission per student per instance — they keep revising the same row, never create a second one

TABLE.NAME: bento_agreements
TABLE.COMMENT: Records that a user has agreed to the plugin's own terms-of-use text (see the 'termsofuse' admin setting) — site-wide, not per-course/instance, since the terms themselves are a single site-wide setting. Checked before any of view.php/edit.php/submission.php/submission_new.php serve their actual content whenever termsofuse is non-empty; skipped entirely when it's empty (no terms configured means nothing to agree to).

FIELD.NAME: termshash
FIELD.COMMENT: sha1 of the termsofuse text at the moment of agreeing — if the admin later edits the wording, this stops matching the CURRENT setting's own hash and the user is asked to agree again, with no manual version number for anyone to remember to bump.

INDEX.NAME: userid_uix
INDEX.COMMENT: One agreement record per user — re-agreeing overwrites the row rather than inserting a second one. No separate foreign key on this same field: Moodle's XMLDB derives the actual database index name from table+field, so a foreign key and a unique index covering the identical single field always collide there regardless of what they're named at the XML level — this index alone is what enforces the invariant that actually matters here.

TABLE.NAME: bento_decks
TABLE.COMMENT: Draft/companion presentations for a teacher's master deck, kept SEPARATE from bento.document (the row driving the activity's own name/settings) rather than being force-merged into it. Each row's own `visible` flag (like bento.documentvisible) independently decides whether it plays as part of the activity's sequence — there is no single exclusive "published" slot; any number of decks (plus bento.document itself, if ITS OWN documentvisible is on) can be visible at once, played through in sortorder. sortorder=0 is never stored here — that's reserved for bento.document itself conceptually sorting first; a row here always represents sortorder>=1.

FIELD.NAME: sortorder
FIELD.COMMENT: 1-based position behind bento.document (which is always conceptually position 0) — lower sorts first. Purely an ordering hint for playback sequence now, not a "which one is published" signal — see this table's own comment.

FIELD.NAME: visible
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether this draft/companion deck is currently part of the activity's own playback sequence — independent of every other row's own visible flag (including bento.documentvisible). Default 0, matching this table's previous semantics where a draft stayed private until explicitly promoted; now it stays private until its own eye toggle is switched on instead.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Teacher-facing label for this draft — the importer's own baseName (e.g. the imported filename), editable.

FIELD.NAME: document
FIELD.COMMENT: LEGACY as of documentinfilestore's own introduction — see that field's comment for the current read/write path.

FIELD.NAME: documentinfilestore
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether this deck's actual content now lives in Moodle's own File API (component mod_bento, filearea BENTO_DECK_FILEAREA, itemid = this row's own id) instead of the `document` text column above — the same scheme bento.documentinfilestore and bento_submissions.documentinfilestore already use, in its OWN filearea (not the main document's own) since bento.id and bento_decks.id come from separate auto-increment sequences and could otherwise collide on the same numeric value. This was the last document type still writing straight into a MySQL text column on every save, a real reliability issue on production infrastructure with a large deck (a direct multi-megabyte UPDATE onto a text column vs. the much cheaper small-row update the file-storage path uses for everything else). 0 (the default) means this row still only has the text-column copy. bento_get_document()/bento_put_document() in lib.php (with their own $filearea parameter) are the one place that decides which of the two a given row is actually read from.

INDEX.NAME: bentoid-sortorder
INDEX.COMMENT: Every read of a bentoid's own drafts is ordered by sortorder — no foreign key on bentoid alone, same collision reasoning as bento_agreements' own userid_uix.
